children: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, Cellectis reported a $101.1M net loss, versus $41.3M in 2025, and $149M in cash and deposits. The company expects funding into the second half of 2028 when its realignment is fully implemented as planned.
Material Details
Detail
AI Analyst View
Nine-month net loss $101.1M vs. $41.3M
The loss widened $59.8M year over year, reflecting higher operating loss despite an improved financial result.
Cash and deposits $149M vs. $211M
Liquidity fell $62M from December 31, 2025; the company expects funding into H2 2028 after planned realignment.
Nine-month revenue and other income $19.9M vs. $67.4M
The $47.5M decline was primarily attributed to lower activity under the AstraZeneca research plans.
R&D expense $108.8M vs. $69.1M
The increase includes $34.9M tied to strategic transformation, including a $26.6M one-off impairment loss.
Headcount reduction of up to 70% expected
The planned reduction may lower costs, but is subject to French works council consultation and labor-law requirements.
.HEAL-101 trial data expected in H2 2027
The China Phase 1 investigator-initiated trial is on track; clinical data could test whether preclinical results translate.
Context by AI Analyst

This report follows Cellectis’ September 2026 strategic shift from cell therapy toward in vivo gene editing, with legacy program discontinuations and restructuring underway. Investors will look for execution of the cost realignment, cash-burn trends, and initial clinical data from .HEAL-101, expected in the second half of 2027.
